audits.title: Completed audit of the use of seclusion in the Approved Centre in Tallaght University Hospital following the introduction of an Integrated Care Pathway
audits.standard: Mental Health Commission rules governing the use of seclusion (13 rules)
audits.setting: Approved Centre (acute psychiatric unit), Tallaght University Hospital

cycle1.period: Before introduction of the Integrated Care Pathway (2012)
cycle1.result: Compliance across the 13 MHC rules ranged from 3% to 100%.

audits.intervention: Seclusion Integrated Care Pathway introduced in 2012 to record and monitor each seclusion episode.

cycle2.result: Compliance ranged from 69% to 100%; 100% compliance with five of the 13 rules.

audits.other_findings: Improvements in medical and nursing reviews, informing patients of reasons and likely duration of seclusion, and informing next of kin. An audit immediately after ICP introduction was also done.
audits.citation: Conlan-Trant R, Corrigan K, Whitty P. Completed audit of the use of seclusion in the Approved Centre in Tallaght University Hospital following the introduction of an Integrated Care Pathway. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S16-S16. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.

audits.title: Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit
audits.setting: Tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit, East London Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Average seclusion 30h; consultant review within 24h under 70%; care plan modification 63%.

audits.intervention: Daily nursing safety huddles, weekly incident reduction meetings and an ongoing QI project on restrictive practice.

cycle2.result: Average seclusion 20h; consultant review within 24h over 90%; care plan modification over 95%; 46 incidents.

audits.other_findings: Just under half of seclusions monitored and documented per Trust guidelines; rapid tranquillisation in 45.7% and restraint in 84.8% of incidents.
audits.citation: Takao Y, Davis F, Saeger I, Ulhaq S, Refaat R. Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S108-S108.

audits.title: QI project: Improvement in quality of Seclusion Medical Review
audits.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE and Trust seclusion policy
audits.setting: Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust inpatient services

cycle1.result: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, mental state and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.

audits.intervention: Seclusion medical review template incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching for doctors.

cycle2.result: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns.

audits.other_findings: Project prompted nurses to audit nursing seclusion reviews.
audits.citation: Shahbaz S, Ward R. QI project: Improvement in quality of Seclusion Medical Review. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S218-S219.

audits.title: Audit Cycle on Medical Reviews of Seclusion in Medium and Low Secure Learning Disability Units
audits.standard: Trust policy 'The use of seclusion and long-term segregation' (SD28), based on Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice (2015) Chapter 26
audits.setting: Medium and low secure learning disability wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Initial medical review within first hour 34%; on-call consultant informed 50%; 4-hourly reviews 50%; RC present at MDT review 67%; medications commented on 20%; risk assessment 48%; reducing restriction 59%

audits.intervention: Education of colleagues working in secure services

cycle2.period: One month of seclusion reviews, three months later
cycle2.result: Initial medical review within first hour 66%; on-call consultant informed 60%; 4-hourly reviews 66%; RC present 100%; medications commented on 72%; observation level 51% (39%); risk assessment 89%; need for continuing seclusion 95% (92%); reducing restriction 84%

audits.other_findings: Physical health was reviewed in 100% in both cycles; 34% (33%) of MDT reviews had only 2 MDT members.
audits.citation: Iyer S, Williamson A. Audit Cycle on Medical Reviews of Seclusion in Medium and Low Secure Learning Disability Units. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S153-S153.

audits.title: Seclusion Pathway Review Audit
audits.standard: Trust seclusion policy and guidelines; target 100% for reviews and documentation
audits.setting: Adult male PICU and adult female mental health ward, Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 100%; initial medical review within 1 hour 81.82% (27); 2-hourly nursing review 93.94% (31); 4-hourly medical review on time in 24 episodes; 8-hour MDT consultant review 78.79% (26); physical observations 100%

audits.other_findings: Missed consultant reviews related to weekend or evening starts; teaching, handbook guidance, posters and re-audit recommended.

audits.standard: Trust seclusion policy: independent seclusion review including an Approved Clinician
audits.setting: Trust-wide, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 83% medical, 11% non-medical ACs, 6% neither; 68% of medical clinicians not AC grade; 0% of non-AC medical reviews documented AC discussion

audits.title: Audit of Seclusion: Evaluating Performance Against National and Local Standards
audits.standard: Trust Seclusion Policy and Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice
audits.setting: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Incident forms completed in 83%, de-escalation attempted in 87%; NEWS incomplete in 82% at initiation. Doctor notified in all but one case (67% within 30 minutes); 100% had medical review, 39% within one hour and 29% after 120 minutes. Internal and external MDTs in 63% and 72%; 11% had neither. Termination reasons reported in 91%.

audits.intervention: None reported yet; recommendations in progress include staff training, policy updates, automated reminders, enhanced documentation, non-touch NEWS and virtual MDT meetings, to be monitored at re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Timing of Site Manager notification unclear in 93.5%. Night-time reviews suspended in 14 cases, 10 because the patient was asleep.
audits.citation: Javaid S, Mittal R, Jabbar Q, Bentley C, Dawson S. Audit of Seclusion: Evaluating Performance Against National and Local Standards. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S246-S247. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10611.

audits.title: Improving the Quality of SHO Seclusion Review Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Mental Health Units (Use of Force) Act 2018; target 80% compliance with all domains
audits.setting: South West London & St George's Mental Health NHS Trust; initial seclusion reviews by resident doctors

cycle1.result: 75% of reviews met all required criteria.

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: seclusion proforma made accessible at handover, proforma circulated by email, teaching in the academic programme, and small-group core trainee teaching.

cycle2.result: 83% of reviews met all required criteria; minimal change in overall compliance on SPC chart.

audits.other_findings: Small numbers and variation between on-call doctors caused wide fluctuations. Risk assessment and physical health documentation improved; authors suggest mandatory completion of all domains.
audits.citation: Wilcha R, Viegas M, Morris L, McCloy-Smith E, Bell D. Improving the Quality of SHO Seclusion Review Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S215-S215. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11515.

audits.title: An Audit on Medical Seclusion Reviews in a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit
audits.standard: SWYT seclusion and long-term segregation policy and seclusion toolkit (medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly reviews, first MDT, independent MDT within 8-18 hours, daily reviews)
audits.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: First MDT within 08:00–22:00 next day 92.7%; out-of-hours reviews adherent 95%; daily non-RC medical reviews 87.2%; independent MDT reviews 24.2%; resident doctor review within 1 hour 64.4%; daily MDT reviews 66.6%.

audits.intervention: Recommended prompts for independent MDT reviews, seclusion toolkit in new doctors' induction and discussion with RCs on documentation.
audits.other_findings: Low daily MDT review figure was linked to incorrect documentation on the seclusion proforma.

audits.title: Seclusion on Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit – Is the Trust Medical Review Policy Being Followed?
audits.standard: Trust seclusion policy: SHO review at 30 minutes, registrar at 8 hours, consultant at 24 hours, then one registrar and one consultant review per subsequent 24 hours
audits.setting: Male Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Springfield Hospital, South West London

cycle1.result: Of 10 episodes lasting over 24 hours, 40% had all required medical reviews documented; 50% had at least one missed or undocumented registrar review; 2 missed consultant reviews

audits.other_findings: Seclusion lasted 8 hours 45 minutes to over 5 days (mean almost 3 days); findings informed an update of the trust seclusion guideline and re-audit is planned.
audits.citation: Scanlon H. Seclusion on Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit – Is the Trust Medical Review Policy Being Followed?. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S180-S180.

audits.title: On-call medical seclusion reviews: are we meeting MHA code of practice (COP) requirements?
audits.standard: MHA Code of Practice chapter 26 (26.133): medical review within 1 hour then 4-hourly with required documentation
audits.setting: Out-of-hours junior trainee seclusion reviews, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: All 56 reviews documented; 49 on time, 4 late with reason, 3 late without; no review mentioned all criteria; risk of self-harm mentioned in 3, side effects in 5, observation levels in 5.

audits.intervention: Results shared at weekly teaching, a Trust-adopted medical seclusion review template, and a seclusion presentation at induction.
audits.other_findings: Higher trainee informed in 53 reviews. Re-audit planned in 12 months.
audits.citation: Turner O, Leung D. On-call medical seclusion reviews: are we meeting MHA code of practice (COP) requirements?. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S109-S109.
